up.name: MODERNA INC
up.company_description: Moderna is a Health Care biotech that sells mRNA vaccines and therapeutics, generating revenue from COVID shots and a pipeline of flu, RSV, and oncology products.
bullets: Aug 19: Merck/Moderna Phase 3 INTerpath-001 (n=1,137) met RFS and DMFS vs Keytruda alone in resected stage IIB–IV melanoma — first positive Phase 3 for an individualized mRNA cancer vaccine.
Shares closed +177% at $174.38 on ~185M volume (vs ~9.6M 3-month avg); 5d +112.5% vs XLV +2.9%. Merck rose ~10% the same day.
Topline gave no Phase 3 hazard ratios; OS not yet mature. Prior Phase 2b KEYNOTE-942 5-year data showed 49% lower recurrence/death risk (HR 0.51) vs Keytruda alone.
Partners will present full data at a medical meeting and engage regulators on filings; no new safety signals vs prior combo studies.
up.ten_day_catalyst: Aug 19 Phase 3 INTerpath-001 win for the Merck-partnered melanoma mRNA vaccine sent shares up about 177%.

Aug 19–20: cancer-AI names rerated after Moderna/Merck’s melanoma Phase 3; BTIG raised TEM PT to $80 from $70 (Buy) on Aug 20.
Jul 20 $1.5B Personalis MRD deal (close late 2026/early 2027) is still a live integration debate. 5d +22.7% vs XLV +2.9%.
up.ten_day_catalyst: Moderna’s melanoma Phase 3 halo plus BTIG lifting its target to $80 extended Tempus’s post-earnings rerating.

down.name: VIKING HOLDINGS
down.company_description: Viking Holdings is a Consumer Discretionary cruise operator selling ocean and river voyages to affluent, destination-focused travelers.
bullets: [2026-08-19] Q2 beat: revenue $2.19B (+16.5% YoY) vs ~$2.14B est; adj. EPS $1.31 vs $1.26; adj. EBITDA $748.4M (+18.2%); net yield $645 (+6.2%). Occupancy slipped to 94.4% from 95.6% YoY.
Pre-print fade from the 2026-08-05 ATH close of $108.26: VIK fell 7.65% on 2026-08-14 (close $97.99) with no company news, after a YTD doubling, as consumer names sold off on weak U.S. retail sales.

Sell-the-news after the beat: 2026-08-19 close $90.77 (intraday as low as ~$90.70). Management said >50% of Q3 river PCDs were hit by Rhine/Danube low water (mid-Jul to mid-Aug) with 10–12% of those sailings canceled and future-cruise vouchers; Q3 opex/revenue hit not quantified.

Bookings still tight as of 2026-08-09: 96% of 2026 core capacity sold ($6.39B advance, +13% vs 2025) and 53% of 2027 despite +15% capacity ($4.71B, +21%). Fuel expense $61.4M vs $43.1M YoY; net leverage 1.2x.
Peer NCLH also −15.7% in the same 5d on yield/leverage; Consumer Discretionary −1.6% vs SPY −1.8% — cruise-idiosyncratic plus sell-the-news, not a booking collapse.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Q2 beat then sell-the-news; Rhine/Danube low water hits Q3; 8/14 fade from ATH.

down.name: ALLEGRO MICROSYSTEMS INC

High-beta analog/auto name riding the chip complex lower; no discrete 5d catalyst beyond sector + mean-reversion from the June peak.

down.name: ALASKA AIR GROUP INC
down.company_description: Alaska Air Group is an Industrials-sector airline operating Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines on West Coast, Hawaii, and transpacific routes.
bullets: Q2 (2026-07-21) still hanging over the tape: adj. loss $0.92 vs ~$0.99 est; revenue ~$4.07B (+10% YoY) slightly light; RASM +8.6%; economic fuel $4.43/gal (+85% YoY) added ~$600M of cost; GAAP net loss $76M. FY guidance remains suspended.

5d price path: 2026-08-14 close $45.96 → 2026-08-19 $41.23. U.S. airline stocks sold off as oil rose on Iran/Hormuz conditions (Investing.com: ALK −2–4% in that session; JetBlue downgrade on Iran fuel risk ~2026-08-17).
Citi reiterated Sell on 2026-08-07 (PT $37); Industrials −3.2% vs SPY −1.8%. Insider sale flagged 2026-08-04. No new earnings in-window — fuel-sensitive name in an oil/airline down-leg.
A 25¢/gal fuel swing is ~50¢ of quarterly EPS per IR; Q3 sits at the low end of the $0–$1 range if fuel averages ~$4/gal.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Iran/Hormuz oil spike hit airlines; Q3 EPS guide $0–$1 vs $1.52 and Hawaii fuel overhang.

down.name: NORWEGIAN CRUISE LINE HOLDINGS LTD
down.company_description: Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings is a Consumer Discretionary cruise operator of the Norwegian, Oceania, and Regent Seven Seas brands.
bullets: [2026-08-18] Mizuho cut NCLH to Neutral from Outperform and PT $22→$17, citing “self-inflicted wounds” (accelerated supply, customer-mix shift, construction delays), ~2–3% next-year EBITDA growth, and a possible >$1B revolver draw plus $2.7B ECA debt that could push leverage above 7x vs ~5.5x YE25.

Balance sheet: $15.0B total debt and 5.3x net leverage at 2026-06-30, $1.5B liquidity. Same-day UBS raised PT $17→$20 (Neutral) — mixed Street, but the Mizuho funding-gap call dominated.
Shares ~$16–17 vs 52-week high $27.18. Peer VIK also −17% in the 5d (sell-the-news/low water); Consumer Discretionary only −1.6% vs SPY −1.8% — cruise yield/leverage, not a broad consumer wipeout.
Q3 yield guide of −8.9% is the near-term fundamental, with Europe itineraries pressured by high airfares and macro; booking curve still “below optimal.”
down.ten_day_catalyst: Mizuho cut to Neutral/$17 on leverage and yields; Q3 net yield guided −8.9%.

up.name: MODERNA INC
up.company_description: Moderna is a Health Care mRNA biotech that commercializes vaccines (COVID, RSV, flu) and develops personalized cancer therapies with Merck.
bullets: On Aug 19, Merck and Moderna said Phase 3 INTerpath-001 (1,137 patients) of intismeran autogene (mRNA-4157/V940) plus KEYTRUDA met RFS and DMFS vs KEYTRUDA alone in resected stage IIB–IV melanoma — the first positive Phase 3 for an mRNA cancer therapy. Investopedia: MRNA +177% that day; BioPharma Dive: ~$45B of market value added; MRK also rose (Investopedia ~12%).

On Aug 5 the FDA approved mFLUSIVA (mRNA-1010) for adults 50+, the first mRNA seasonal-flu vaccine and Moderna’s fifth product (fourth FDA). Supply is slated for the 2026–27 season; ≥65 approval is accelerated pending a postmarketing study.

The Phase 3 readout builds on KEYNOTE-942 5-year ASCO 2026 data: 49% lower risk of recurrence or death (HR 0.51) and 59% lower distant-metastasis risk (HR 0.41) vs KEYTRUDA alone. The companies will file with regulators; OS is still immature.
Health Care returned +7.3% vs SPY +3.5% over the 20d window; MRNA’s +137% is almost entirely the cancer-trial day plus the earlier flu approval, not a sector beta move.
up.ten_day_catalyst: Aug 19 Phase 3 melanoma-vaccine win with Merck more than doubled the stock; Aug 5 FDA approved mRNA flu.

See the wiki entry for Cloud/Data Center mix, Rovo, Atlassian Ascend and prior FY26 quarters.

up.name: RINGCENTRAL INC CLASS A
up.company_description: RingCentral is an IT-sector UCaaS and CCaaS vendor selling cloud phone, video and contact-center subscriptions plus AI voice agents.
bullets: On 23 Jul 2026 RNG reported Q2 revenue $657M (+5.9% YoY) and subscriptions $634M (+5.8%), both above the high end of guide; non-GAAP EPS $1.22 vs ~$1.07–$1.16 Street; GAAP OM 7.7% and non-GAAP OM 23.4%.
Free cash flow $180M (+24.8% YoY, 27.4% margin). Raised FY26 revenue to $2.635–$2.646B and FCF to $615–$625M; Q3 guide $664–$670M revenue and $1.25–$1.30 non-GAAP EPS.

Board hiked the quarterly dividend ~67% to $0.125 (payable 20 Aug). Paid AI products now 13% of ARR, doubled YoY; same day it expanded an OpenAI collaboration and a multi-year NiCE resale of RingEX UCaaS.
Stock surged ~25% on 24 Jul, accounting for the bulk of the 20-day +56.3% move in a UCaaS/CCaaS name that had been a long-duration laggard.
up.ten_day_catalyst: 23 Jul Q2 beat, FCF raise to $615–625M, 67% dividend hike and OpenAI/NiCE deals.

up.name: PAYCOM SOFTWARE INC
up.company_description: Paycom is an Industrials-sector HCM software vendor that sells a single-database payroll, HR, and talent suite to mid-market employers on a recurring SaaS model.
bullets: Aug 5 Q2: revenue $531.2M (+9.8% YoY) beat by ~$18M; recurring/other $505.2M (+11.0%). GAAP EPS $2.34 vs $1.58 LY; non-GAAP EPS $2.78 vs ~$2.38 Street; adj. EBITDA $235M (44% margin).
Raised FY26: total revenue $2.197–2.212B (7–8% YoY) from $2.175–2.195B; recurring growth 8–9% (was 7–8%); adj. EBITDA $1.007–1.022B (~46% midpoint margin). Client-funds interest ~$105M.
Q2 capital return: 2.57M shares bought for $345.9M plus $17.9M dividends. H1 FCF $373M (33.8% margin). Cash $198M vs $900M long-term debt at Jun 30.
Print sparked a multi-day HCM rally (reports of ~6% to ~23% one-day pops depending on close); Simply Wall St later pegged the post-print move at +31% into Aug 9.
up.ten_day_catalyst: Aug 5 Q2 beat ($531M, +11% recurring) and FY26 raise to $2.197–$2.212B drove a multi-day rally.

up.name: CARIS LIFE SCIENCES INC
up.company_description: Caris Life Sciences is a Health Care diagnostics company that sells molecular profiling and oncology tests using whole-exome and transcriptome sequencing.
bullets: On Aug 5 Caris reported Q2 revenue of $263.7M, +45% YoY, with molecular-profiling services at $252.3M (+55%) on ~59,200 clinical cases (+18% YoY), including ~48,300 MI Profile and ~10,700 Caris Assure cases.
The P&L inflected: net loss narrowed to $0.6M from $71.8M a year earlier, adjusted EBITDA was +$55.7M, operating cash flow $28.5M, free cash flow $6.4M, and gross margin 68% (+~500 bps YoY).

Management raised FY26 revenue guidance to $1.03–$1.04B (27–28% growth) from $1.00–$1.02B and reaffirmed ~20% clinical therapy-selection volume growth. QuiverQuant: shares +17.9% on Aug 6 after the print.

Operating highlights in the same release: Caris Detect multi-cancer early-detection blood test launched, MolDX approval for ChromoSeq myeloid whole-genome profiling, and a $100M buyback with ~$82.1M remaining. Health Care +7.3% vs CAI +60% over the window.
up.ten_day_catalyst: Aug 5 Q2 beat-and-raise: $264M revenue (+45%) and FY26 guide lifted to $1.03–$1.04B.

up.name: UNITY SOFTWARE INC
up.company_description: Unity Software is an IT-sector game-engine and ads platform that sells Create tools to developers and Grow/Unity Vector AI advertising to mobile publishers.
bullets: Aug 6 Q2 print: revenue $546.5M (+24% YoY) vs ~$515M consensus; adj. EPS $0.28 vs $0.22; adj. EBITDA $160M (29% margin, +77% YoY); FCF $202M.
Strategic Grow revenue $329M (+63% YoY) on Unity Vector AI, which management said hit a $1B annual run-rate two quarters early; Vector +23% QoQ.
Q3 guide: strategic revenue $540–550M (+44–47% YoY), Grow $380–385M (+68–70%); adj. EBITDA $185–190M (implied ~33% margin). GAAP net-income profitability pulled forward to Q3 from Q4.
Non-strategic revenue fell 33% after the Apr 30 ironSource Ads sunset; Supersonic publishing was sold Aug 4. Shares +15.1% the session after the print (close $40.81).
up.ten_day_catalyst: Aug 6 Q2 beat plus Vector AI $1B run-rate and GAAP profit pulled to Q3; stock +15% next day.

up.name: UIPATH INC CLASS A
up.company_description: UiPath is an Information Technology software vendor that sells enterprise robotic-process-automation and agentic-AI orchestration subscriptions.
bullets: PATH had no earnings in the window (Q2 FY27 is due Sep 3). The 20d started at the Jul 23 close near $10.20 after a late-July dip; Tickeron/StocksToTrade: the stock then ran to about $16.68 on Aug 13 (~57%) before settling near $16.
On Aug 7 PATH rose ~7% to $14.93 alongside Palantir (+10%) and C3.ai (+5%) as the agentic-AI software cohort re-rated together (24/7 Wall St.).

On Aug 14 RBC’s Matthew Hedberg kept Sector Perform but raised the PATH target to $15 from $12, citing more constructive software channel checks and a ~30% bounce since the May 28 Q1 print ($418.4M revenue, +17% YoY; non-GAAP EPS $0.15).

Sector rotation did the heavy lifting: Seeking Alpha (Aug 4) had IGV +7.64% vs SMH −7.91% as money rotated out of chips into beaten-down software. IT returned only +2.7% vs SPY +3.5% over the 20d, so PATH’s +56% is a high-beta SaaS catch-up, not an earnings print.
up.ten_day_catalyst: Software-vs-semis rotation and the agentic-AI cohort rally lifted PATH off the Jul 23 $10.20 low.

up.name: WORKDAY INC CLASS A
up.company_description: Workday is an Information Technology cloud-software company that sells subscription HCM and financial-management applications to large enterprises.
bullets: On Aug 13 Reuters reported Silver Lake is in talks to take Workday private (pre-deal mkt cap ~$43B). Shares jumped ~18% to about $206–$208 — the best day since 2016 — with multiple volatility halts and mkt cap near $51B. Neither side confirmed a deal.

That M&A headline sat on a software-sector bounce after the early-2026 “SaaSpocalypse”: Tickeron put WDAY up ~35% from $147 on Jul 20 after a June low near $113. IT +2.7% vs WDAY +54% over the 20d window.

Post-spike Street split: BofA lifted its PT to $205 from $140 (Neutral), Barclays Overweight $200, UBS to $220; Deutsche Bank and BTIG cut to Hold/Neutral on valuation. FY Q2 2027 results are Aug 27 (Street ~$2.3–$2.6 EPS, ~$2.6B revenue).

Last fundamental print was May 21 Q1 FY27: non-GAAP EPS $2.66 vs ~$2.25–$2.51, revenue $2.54B, subscription +14% to $2.35B, non-GAAP OM guide 30.5% — but that was before this 20d window; the Aug 13 buyout rumor is the window’s driver.
up.ten_day_catalyst: Aug 13 Reuters: Silver Lake talks to take Workday private sent shares up ~18%, best day since 2016.

up.name: PROCORE TECHNOLOGIES INC
up.company_description: Procore is an Information Technology SaaS company that sells construction-management software subscriptions to contractors, owners, and specialty trades.
bullets: After the close on Jul 29, Q2 revenue was $375M, +16% YoY (prior Q2 guide $364–$366M; Street ~$366M). First GAAP operating profit: 1% margin, net income $16.9M, GAAP EPS $0.11; non-GAAP OM 21% and non-GAAP EPS $0.47 vs ~$0.33–$0.42.

Cash and backlog: operating cash $88M (+185% YoY), FCF $65M (+507% YoY). Remaining performance obligations $1.67B, +24% YoY. $100k+ ARR organic customers 2,871 (+14% YoY); gross revenue retention 95%.

Guide raise: FY26 revenue $1.510–$1.514B (14.5% at the high end) vs prior $1.499–$1.503B; non-GAAP OM 18.5–19.0% and FCF margin 19.5%. Q3 $382–$384M (~13.3% YoY). FY27 non-GAAP OM target 25%. StockTitan: +7.2% around the print.

The rest of the +52% 20d move tracks the same August software-vs-semis rotation that lifted PATH/WDAY (IGV up, SMH down early August; IT only +2.7%). Construction SaaS re-rated on the GAAP-profit milestone plus the sector bid.
up.ten_day_catalyst: Jul 29 Q2 beat with first GAAP profit and a FY26 raise, then the August software rotation.

down.name: MONSTER BEVERAGE CORP
down.company_description: Monster Beverage is a Consumer Staples energy-drink maker that sells Monster, Reign, Bang and Coke-acquired brands worldwide, plus a small alcohol portfolio.
bullets: The −53% 20d / −49% 5d print is the Aug 11 2-for-1 split, not a collapse: new shares distributed after the Aug 10 close; unadjusted quotes halved (e.g. ~$91 prior close → $45.71 on Aug 11, −49.8%). Record date was July 24; sixth split since 2005. Market cap stayed ~$90B.

Aug 6 Q2 (pre-split) was a beat: net sales $2.54B (+20.2% YoY; +17.9% FX-neutral) vs ~$2.43B; GAAP EPS $0.59 / adj. $0.60 vs ~$0.58. Net income $584.5M (+19.6%). International sales $1.16B (+34.6%) reached 46% of the mix (from 41%).

Monster Energy drinks $2.36B (+21.6%); Strategic Brands $143.7M (+10.6%); Alcohol Brands $32.2M (−15.2%). Gross margin 55.9% vs 55.7%; opex 26.8% of sales (vs 25.8%) as selling spend rose to $269.2M from $196.9M.
No repurchase in Q2; ~$900M remained authorized as of Aug 5. Split-adjusted trading around $46 is consistent with the pre-split ~$91–$96 tape, so the Russell rank is a corporate-action artifact.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Aug 11 2-for-1 split halved the unadjusted quote; Aug 6 Q2 was a beat, not a collapse.

down.name: CH ROBINSON WORLDWIDE INC
down.company_description: C.H. Robinson is an Industrials freight broker that matches shippers with truckload, LTL and global-forwarding capacity and earns a spread on each load.
bullets: Jul 23 Dallas County jury returned a $604M advisory verdict in Lipe v. Lupus Superior (2021 I-20 crash; three dead). CHRW assigned 23% fault (~$139M several) but treated as the driver’s employer, so joint-and-several on the full award. First major post-Montgomery (May 2026) broker-liability case. Stock −9.25% Jul 24 to $186.50 from a $210.33 52-week high two days earlier.
10-Q: $155M liability/excess insurance per occurrence, $5M deductible; only an immaterial accrual; company will appeal. Peers RXO and LSTR sold off with it.

Jul 29 Q2 beat the P&L: revenue $4.93B (+19.3%) vs ~$4.35B; adj. EPS $1.61 (+24.8%) vs ~$1.53; adj. op. income $263.2M (+19.5%). NAST volume +1.5% vs Cass −3.3% (13th straight outgrowth). Operating cash flow collapsed to $35.9M from $227.1M (−$191.2M) on working-capital/rate expansion.

Jul 30 session −15.4% to ~$146.92 despite the beat: trough-cycle volume, the cash-flow swing, and residual verdict risk. Two-wave 20d: verdict then print, taking shares from the $210 high into the high-$140s.
down.ten_day_catalyst: July 23 $604M Texas nuclear verdict and July 29 cash-flow miss crushed the stock in two waves.

down.name: ALLEGRO MICROSYSTEMS INC
down.company_description: Allegro MicroSystems is an Information Technology-sector analog-chip maker selling magnetic sensors and power ICs into auto, industrial, and data-center markets.
bullets: Jul 30 Q1 FY27 (ended Jun 26): sales $259.2M (+27% YoY, +7% QoQ) and non-GAAP EPS $0.23 beat ~$0.21 / ~$251M consensus; auto $165M (+15% YoY, only +1% QoQ), industrial $94M (+59% YoY). Data center hit a record 17% of sales (+32% QoQ).

Q2 FY27 guide was modest vs the multiple: sales $265–$275M and non-GAAP EPS $0.23–$0.26; mgmt said auto/industrial grow only mid-single-digit sequentially and data-center sequential growth would not stay in the +20% range. Shares −3.6% on the print after an ~8% drop on Jul 24–25.

IT sector +2.7% over the window vs ALGM −26.1%. Stock is ~45% below the $69.62 Jun 30 close; Trefis attributes the de-rating to a P/S compression from 10.7x to 7.7x as analog/AI-semi multiples unwound.
Mizuho cut its PT to $58 from $67 on Jul 31 (still Outperform). The 20d move is a high-multiple reset after a beat-and-decelerate guide, not a fundamental miss.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Q1 FY27 beat, but a modest Q2 guide and analog/AI-semi de-rating from June highs.

down.name: AAON INC
down.company_description: AAON is an Industrials-sector HVAC manufacturer that sells custom rooftop units and BASX liquid-cooling systems to commercial and data-center customers.
bullets: Aug 10 Q2: record sales $627.0M (+101% YoY; ~+22% vs consensus) and GAAP/adj EPS $0.68/$0.69 vs ~$0.51. BASX-branded sales $345M (+216%); AAON brand $282M (+39%). Coil Products (liquid cooling) sales $147M, GM only 16.0%.

Raised FY26 sales growth to 55–60% from 40–45% but cut gross-margin outlook to 25–26% from 27–28%. Q2 GM 24.3% vs 26.6% a year ago; Memphis overhead $18.1M vs $3.0M YoY. Shares −5.9% on the print and about −10% into the next session.

Backlog $2.0B (+98% YoY) but −7.4% sequentially as BASX conversion outran new awards. Mgmt still cites a healthy data-center pipeline; the market treated the sequential dip plus the GM reset as the story.

HVAC peer LII had already crashed ~20% on Jul 29 after cutting EPS on residential weakness. Industrials −1.2% over the window vs AAON −25%; this is a sector multiple compression plus a company-specific margin cut, not a demand collapse.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Record Q2 and a raised sales guide, offset by a 200-bp GM cut and sequential backlog dip.

down.name: MASTEC INC
down.company_description: MasTec is an Industrials-sector infrastructure contractor that engineers and builds communications, power-delivery, pipeline, and clean-energy projects in North America.
bullets: Jul 30 Q2: revenue $4.37B (+23.4% YoY, beat ~$4.31B) but adj EPS $2.22 vs $2.23 Street; adj EBITDA $384M in line at 8.8% margin. Shares −10.9% after the print, then another −17.7% session by Aug 1 as the FY adj-EPS raise to $9.30 (from ~$8.79 prior) lagged Street.
Record 18-month backlog $21.4B (+30% YoY, +$1.1B QoQ). Clean Energy & Infrastructure revenue +43%; Communications EBITDA margin −170 bps to 8.2%. Q2 free cash flow −$59M.
Closed the $1.65B Superior Group data-center electrical deal in late July (~$1.175B cash / $475M stock). Aug 6 priced $650M senior notes due 2036 to refinance acquisition-related debt (close Aug 17).
Q3 guide $4.93B revenue / $2.98 adj EPS; FY $18.2B / $9.30 adj EPS. The 20d drop is a guidance/Street-gap and deal-financing reset, not a backlog break.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Q2 adj-EPS miss and FY guide below Street, plus $650M notes for the Superior deal.

down.name: DAVITA INC
down.company_description: DaVita is a Health Care dialysis operator running U.S. and international outpatient kidney-care centers plus risk-based integrated-care contracts.
bullets: Aug 4 Q2: revenue $3.554B; diluted EPS $4.02 vs ~$3.88 Street (and $2.58 LY); operating income $579M (16.3% margin); FCF $256M. Bought 2.2M shares at $154.95 avg ($348M).
U.S. treatments 7.23M; per-day +1.09% seq / normalized non-acquired +0.3% YoY. Revenue per treatment $415.87, −$1.72 seq on weaker commercial/ACA mix and lower phosphate-binder revenue.
Reaffirmed FY26 adj. OI $2.15–$2.25B, adj. EPS $14.10–$15.20 (midpoint $14.65 vs ~$14.88 Street), FCF $1.00–$1.25B. Volume now expected near the top of +25–50 bps; H2 RPT slightly negative.
Call flagged a ~$40M 2026 commercial-mix headwind and ~$70M more in 2027 from ACA subsidy roll-off. Tape: ~6% to ~19% post-print drops depending on source as mix/RPT, not the EPS beat, set the price.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Aug 4 EPS beat, but sequential RPT decline and FY midpoint below Street hit the stock hard.

down.name: LENNOX INTERNATIONAL INC
down.company_description: Lennox International is an Industrials-sector HVACR manufacturer selling heating, cooling, and refrigeration equipment to residential and commercial customers.
bullets: Jul 29 Q2: sales $1.545B (+3% YoY) missed ~$1.6B Street; GAAP EPS $7.72 (in line with $7.61–$7.76). Home Comfort $936M (−7% YoY) with unit volumes −12%; Building Climate Solutions $610M (+24%, +15% organic, +9% M&A).
Cut FY26 EPS to $23.00–$24.00 from $23.50–$25.00 (Street ~$24.52); reaffirmed ~8% revenue growth but now 5 pts M&A / ~3 pts organic. Home Comfort FY growth cut to ~1% from ~4%.

Shares tumbled ~20% on Jul 29 (largest one-day drop since 2001). Goldman cut PT to $547 from $625 on Jul 31. Residential new-construction and replacement softness, not data-center cooling, is the driver.
Same HVAC-sector de-rating later hit AAON (data-center cooling) even after a beat-and-raise. Industrials −1.2% vs LII −24.7% over the window.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Residential HVAC volume miss and a FY EPS cut to $23–$24; shares −20% on the print.

down.name: DUTCH BROS INC CLASS A
down.company_description: Dutch Bros is a Consumer Discretionary drive-thru coffee chain selling handcrafted beverages through company-operated and franchised shops.
bullets: Aug 5 Q2: revenue $550.9M (+32.5% YoY) vs ~$525M Street; adj. EPS $0.33 vs $0.29; adj. EBITDA $113.7M (+27.8%) but margin −76 bps to 20.6%. Opened 48 shops (1,225 system at Jun 30).

Company-operated comps +8.3% (transactions +3.4% / ticket ~+4.9 pts); system comps +5.8% but system transactions only +1.7%. Management said H2 pricing adds <1 pt to ticket after a July increase rolled off.
Raised FY26: revenue $2.10–$2.13B, system comps 5–6% (trending midpoint), adj. EBITDA $385–$390M; capex lifted to $350–$370M, including a Phoenix franchise buy (~31 shops / $63.5M).
Stock fell ~16–19% Aug 6 (one tape to $53.33) as investors treated ticket-heavy comps, slower franchise traffic, and a bigger capex bill as the story, not the beat/raise.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Aug 5 beat and FY raise, but ticket-heavy comps and a capex hike sent shares down ~19%.

down.name: UNDER ARMOUR INC CLASS C
down.company_description: Under Armour Class C is a Consumer Discretionary performance-apparel brand selling athletic clothing, footwear and accessories through wholesale and DTC.
bullets: Same company as UAA: Aug 7 Q1 FY27 (ended Jun 30) revenue $1.10B (−3%; −4% cc) vs ~$1.11B. NA −9% to $610M; international +5% to $490M (EMEA +12%, APAC −7%/−10% cc, LatAm +8%). Footwear −8%, eComm −12%, DTC −6%.

Gross margin 54.1% (+590 bps) almost entirely from IEEPA tariff refunds booked in FY26. GAAP EPS $0.00; adj. EPS $0.05. Op. income $47M / adj. $52M. Inventory $1.1B (−3%); cash $396M after retiring the 2026 notes.

FY27 revenue cut to a mid-single-digit decline from a prior “slight decline”: NA now MSD down (was LSD), APAC and EMEA now LSD down (were LSD up). Adj. operating income held at $140–160M and adj. EPS at $0.08–$0.12; GAAP LPS now $0.01–$0.05.

Shares had rallied ~30% into mid-July (~$7.43 on Jul 18). Print-day reaction was about −6% premarket / −7% session low / −4.5% EOD; the 20d −28.5% is that cut plus the pre-print rally unwinding into ~$5.25–$5.36.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Aug 7 FY27 revenue-guide cut to a mid-single-digit decline unwound a pre-print rally.

down.name: APPLOVIN CORP CLASS A
down.company_description: AppLovin is an IT-sector mobile-ad platform that monetizes publisher inventory via its Axon AI recommendation engine.
bullets: Aug 5 Q2: revenue $1.924B (+53% YoY) vs ~$1.94B Street and below the $1.915–$1.945B guide midpoint; diluted EPS $3.76 in-line; adj. EBITDA $1.614B (84% margin, +58% YoY); FCF $863M.

Q3 guide $2.055–$2.085B revenue (46–48% YoY / 7–8% seq) and adj. EBITDA $1.71–$1.74B (83% margin) — slightly below ~$2.08B Street. CEO Foroughi blamed 'lighter than normal' gaming-model upgrades that landed after quarter-end.
Consumer advertiser spend hit a record, ~28% above the Q4 2025 peak; $551M buybacks/withholdings in Q2. CNBC/IBD: shares −19–20% Aug 6 to a 52-week low (~$336).
Not the same driver as TTD: APP is a tiny miss on still-53% growth; TTD printed +3% and guided Q3 to $650M. Adtech sentiment was shared; fundamentals were not.
See the wiki entry.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Aug 5 Q2 revenue miss vs own guide and a slightly light Q3 outlook sent shares ~20% lower.
